mechanism: Both drugs have anticholinergic properties; benztropine is directly anticholinergic while isotretinoin can potentiate anticholinergic effects, increasing risk of xerostomia, constipation, and urinary retention.
action: Monitor for additive anticholinergic effects; counsel patient on adequate hydration and bowel regimen; consider alternative to benztropine if anticholinergic burden becomes problematic during isotretinoin therapy.
